tags.chapter_name: Center of Mass Momentum and Collision

question.text: The distance of centre of mass from end <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math> of a one dimensional rod <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mrow><mi>A</mi><mi>B</mi></mrow></mfenced></math> having mass density <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>ρ</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mfenced><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>-</mo><mfrac><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><msup><mi>L</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mfrac></mrow></mfenced><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> and length <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>L</mi></math> (in meter) is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mrow><mn>3</mn><mi>L</mi></mrow><mi>α</mi></mfrac><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>α</mi></math> is _____ (where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> is the distance form end <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math>)

solution.text:
Given here:

Mass density, ρ=ρ01-x2L2 kg m-1

Let us suppose there is an element of length dx at a distance x from left must end.

Mass of this element is dm=ρdx=ρ01-x2L2

The centre of mass of this element is Xcm=∫xdm∫dm

=ρ0∫0lx-x2L2xdx∫0lρ01-x2L2dx

=L22-L44L2L-L33L2=L242L3=3L8

Hence, the value of α=8.
